title: Number of 1 Bits
description: Given a non-negative integer `n`, return the number of `1` bits in its binary representation (also called its Hamming weight).

complexity.time: O(k) where k is the number of set bits

hints: You can inspect one bit at a time with n & 1 followed by a right shift.
That takes up to 31 steps even for sparse numbers. Is there a trick that removes just one set bit per step?
n & (n - 1) clears the lowest set bit. Count how many times you can apply it before n becomes 0.

solution.explanation: Subtracting 1 from n flips the lowest set bit to 0 and turns all the zeros below it into ones, so n & (n - 1) clears exactly the lowest set bit. Repeat until n is 0 and count the iterations, which equals the number of set bits. That is O(k) for k set bits (at most 31), with O(1) space.
